rationale: The new results complete the qualification requested by the previous decision. At S_eta=1000, the 256² CFL=0.8 trajectory reached the observation window in 103.6 seconds, versus 191.3 seconds at CFL=0.4; the reported rate difference is about 0.18%. The 384² trajectory also reached the window in 316.7 seconds, with a reported rate change of about 0.22% and minimum sheet FWHM increasing from eight to ten cells. Sampled conservation and diagnostic checks provide useful qualification, subject to their recorded limitations. These exploratory results demonstrate an affordable trajectory and refinement at one resistivity, not resolved full-range scaling or an accepted scientific claim. The worker's response to the earlier replan has therefore produced useful progress, and further timing polish at this case is unnecessary. Budget feasibility remains at risk: approximately 2089 seconds remain, endpoint refinement costs are unmeasured, the high-S base result has only four sheet-width cells, and no methods review is recorded. Continuing into methods review and a measured-cost production plan follows the previous decision; it does not authorize an unqualified full batch.
